{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-al-d","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"fcdc9703d427f69028d5f82521fa42cee2c4a24dac09ff653434e82efb76e110","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-al-class-d:lineage:19","source_registry_sha256":"ea8231e949706ecda9f2a398d6eaf9ab30e224ac7defb0e6291b764b84ed0d95","source_liveness_sha256":"e524456f547beacfeca0647b02ef401523e58aa5b835501e7cbdd821b6546315"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Large vehicles, parking and restraint laws","heading":"C — Large vehicles, parking and restraint laws","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — Large vehicles, parking and restraint laws

FACT_ID: sec05-F01 | anchor: A29
Whoever is legally at fault, the motorcyclist is usually the one who loses in a car-motorcycle crash, and alert drivers who watch for riders can reduce those crashes, injuries and deaths. [A29]
Source: [A29 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec05-F02 | anchor: A29
No-Zones are the areas around trucks and buses where crashes are most likely, and some of them are blind spots in which a car vanishes from the large-vehicle driver's view. [A29]
Source: [A29 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec05-F03 | anchor: A29
Trucks and buses have big blind spots on both sides, so if you cannot see the driver's face in the side mirror, that driver cannot see you either. [A29]
Why it matters: a mirror works both ways; no face in the mirror means you are hidden in a side No-Zone.
Source: [A29 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec05-F04 | anchor: A29
Pass a truck or bus on the left and as quickly as you can, moving fully ahead of it so the driver can see you, and never cruise alongside it. [A29]
Source: [A29 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec05-F05 | anchor: A29
The rear No-Zone directly behind a truck or bus can stretch as far as 200 feet, so a tailgating car is hidden from the driver, cannot see ahead, and has no escape if the big vehicle brakes hard. [A29]
Source: [A29 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec05-F06 | anchor: A29
Dim your headlights whenever you follow a large vehicle at night, because bright beams bounce off its side mirrors and blind its driver. [A29]
Source: [A29 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec05-F07 | anchor: A30
After passing a large vehicle, do not cut back in too soon: wait until its entire front shows in your rear-view mirror, and keep your speed up once you are in front of it. [A30]
Why it matters: slowing down right after moving in front of a truck takes away the stopping room it needs.
Source: [A30 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec05-F08 | anchor: A30
Truck and bus drivers need close to twice as much room to stop as car drivers do. [A30]
Source: [A30 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec05-F09 | anchor: A30
A National Safety Council study cited in the manual found that a loaded truck traveling 55 miles per hour needs 430 feet to stop safely, compared with 193 feet for a passenger car. [A30]
Source: [A30 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec05-F10 | anchor: A30
Never cross behind a truck or bus that is backing up, because drivers of large vehicles cannot see directly behind them and may not see you at all. [A30]
Source: [A30 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec05-F11 | anchor: A30
To make a right turn safely, a truck or bus driver has to swing wide to the left first, which opens a gap on the right that can become a squeeze play. [A30]
Source: [A30 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec05-F12 | anchor: A30
While a large vehicle's right turn signal is blinking, do not try to pass it on the right; the driver cannot see you and you could be trapped, so wait until the turn is finished. [A30]
Why it matters: the wide left swing looks like room to pass on the right, but it is the trap the manual warns about.
Source: [A30 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec05-F13 | anchor: A30
Any vehicle you leave standing beside a rural highway, whatever the reason, has to be moved off the paved or main traveled part of the road, and if it cannot be moved you must use lights and markings to warn other traffic. [A30]
Source: [A30 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec05-F14 | anchor: A30
When you park on a hill, always set the hand brake and shift into park, or into reverse or low gear if the car has no park position, so it cannot roll into traffic if the brakes fail. [A30]
Source: [A30 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec05-F15 | anchor: A30
Parked facing downhill beside a curb, turn your front wheels toward the curb and shift into reverse or park. [A30]
Source: [A30 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec05-F16 | anchor: A30
Parked facing uphill beside a curb, turn your front wheels away from the curb and shift into low gear or park. [A30]
Why it matters: uphill with a curb is the only case where the wheels point away from the curb.
Source: [A30 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec05-F17 | anchor: A30
Where there is no curb, turn the wheels toward the edge of the road, whether the car faces uphill or downhill. [A30]
Source: [A30 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec05-F18 | anchor: A31
You may not park inside an intersection, on a crosswalk, or on a sidewalk. [A31]
Source: [A31 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec05-F19 | anchor: A31
Parking is banned within 20 feet of a crosswalk at an uncontrolled intersection. [A31]
Source: [A31 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec05-F20 | anchor: A31
Parking is banned within 30 feet of a stop sign, a flashing beacon or a traffic control signal placed at the roadside. [A31]
Source: [A31 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec05-F21 | anchor: A31
Parking is banned within 50 feet of the nearest rail of a railroad crossing. [A31]
Source: [A31 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec05-F22 | anchor: A31
Parking is banned within 15 feet of a fire hydrant. [A31]
Why it matters: the hydrant gap is the shortest distance on the list, so it is easy to mix up with the crosswalk gap.
Source: [A31 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec05-F23 | anchor: A31
You may not park in front of a driveway, on any bridge, or inside a tunnel. [A31]
Source: [A31 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec05-F24 | anchor: A31
Double parking is not allowed: you may not park on the roadway side of a vehicle already parked at the curb or the edge of the highway. [A31]
Source: [A31 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec05-F25 | anchor: A31
You may not park beside a curb painted yellow or anywhere official signs forbid parking. [A31]
Source: [A31 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec05-F26 | anchor: A31
To parallel park, pull up even with the parked car ahead of the space, ease back gently toward the space, turn the wheels sharply, begin straightening them, and finish with the wheels parallel to the curb. [A31]
Source: [A31 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec05-F27 | anchor: A32
Alabama's safety belt law requires every occupant of the vehicle to be restrained, no matter how old they are. [A32]
Source: [A32 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec05-F28 | anchor: A32
A seat belt works best when it is pulled snug across the hip bones. [A32]
Source: [A32 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0032]

Glossary: No-Zone — a danger area around a truck or bus where crashes are likely, often a blind spot [A29]. Squeeze play — the trap on the right side of a truck or bus that swings left before turning right [A30]. Double parking — parking on the roadway side of a car already parked at the curb [A31].
Memory aid: downhill or no curb, wheels go toward the edge; only uphill with a curb turns them away [A30].
